newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia Senate approves limited extradition bill.
newsitem.headline: Colombia Senate approves limited extradition bill.

text.p: Colombia's Senate on Thursday approved a controversial bill that would partially lift the country's six-year-old ban on the extradition of drug traffickers and other criminals.
A plenary session voted 53-14 in favour of the bill, which still faces six more congressional hurdles and if successful would only make its way on to the statue books at the end of this year.

But critics say the original government-sponsored bill has been so watered down that it is virtually useless and is unlikely to cut any ice with U.S. anti-drug officials who have been urging the Colombia government to push through a tough extradition law through Congress.

The bill, if it makes it way intact through six more congressional debates, would forbid the extradition of alleged criminals if they surrender to the Colombian authorities or if they face tougher penalties abroad than they would under the notoriously lenient Colombian justice system.

The vote came on the day Virgilio Barco, former president who led his country through one of the most violent periods of drug-related violence in the nation's troubled history, was buried following his death on Tuesday.

Barco, president between 1986 and 1990, is the only Colombian leader to have ordered the extradition of one of the country's top drug lords to the United States. He sent Carlos Lehder, one of the masterminds of the infamous Medellin drug mob, to face trial in the United States in 1987.
